title: Rotating stratified and shallow-water mathematical models

items.title: Rotating stratified and shallow-water equation families
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; cross-batch interfaces inspected, but the upstream supplier readiness record is missing.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval. For $d=2,3$, define the flat periodic domain $\mathbb T^d:=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ and integrate over the fundamental cell $Q_d=[0,2\pi]^d$ using ordinary Lebesgue measure. A field on $\mathbb T^d$ is represented by its $2\pi$-periodic lift to the nonempty open spatial domain $\mathbb R^d$. All fields below are classical: their displayed time and spatial derivatives are continuous, and the velocity and buoyancy fields have continuous second spatial derivatives. Each displayed equation is a pointwise equality.

For a scalar field $q$, set $\nabla q=(\partial_{x_1}q,\ldots,\partial_{x_d}q)$ and $\Delta q=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}^2q$. For a vector field $w=(w_1,\ldots,w_d)$, set $\nabla\cdot w=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}w_j$, $\Delta w=(\Delta w_1,\ldots,\Delta w_d)$, $|w|^2=\sum_{j=1}^dw_j^2$, and $|\nabla w|^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^d(\partial_{x_j}w_i)^2$. For a matrix field $A$, its divergence is rowwise: $(\nabla\cdot A)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}A_{ij}$. In three dimensions $e_3\times u=(-u_2,u_1,0)$, and in two dimensions $Jv=(-v_2,v_1)$.

On $\mathbb T^3$, let $u:I\times\mathbb T^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be velocity, $b:I\times\mathbb T^3\to\mathbb R$ be a buoyancy perturbation, and $\pi:I\times\mathbb T^3\to\mathbb R$ be specific pressure. Let $e_3=(0,0,1)$, and prescribe constant parameters $f\in\mathbb R$, $N>0$, and $\nu,\kappa\ge0$. The rotating, linear, constant-stratification Boussinesq equation family is

$$u_t+f e_3\times u+\nabla\pi=b e_3+\nu\Delta u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,\qquad b_t+N^2u_3=\kappa\Delta b.$$

Here $\Delta$ acts componentwise, $u_3$ is the vertical velocity component, $f$ is the Coriolis coefficient, $N$ is the constant buoyancy-frequency parameter, and $\nu$ and $\kappa$ are the prescribed momentum and buoyancy diffusion coefficients. The inviscid branch is the choice $\nu=\kappa=0$. In the Boussinesq interpretation, a constant reference density is used in inertia and the divergence constraint while the density anomaly is retained through the vertical buoyancy force; small fractional density variation is an applicability assumption, not a theorem giving a compressible limit.

For its rotating-frame interpretation, take a time-dependent orthonormal Euclidean basis rotating uniformly about $e_3$ with constant angular velocity $\boldsymbol\Omega=\Omega e_3$, so $f=2\Omega$. The Coriolis acceleration on the force side is $-2\boldsymbol\Omega\times u$, written on the left as $+f e_3\times u$. If $\Phi$ is gravitational potential per unit mass, define the effective potential by $\Phi_{\rm eff}(x):=\Phi(x)-\tfrac12|\boldsymbol\Omega\times x|^2$, which absorbs the centrifugal contribution. These frame and effective-potential choices are assumptions; the inertial-frame balance is distinct. The periodic domain is a mathematical idealization, not a claim that the physical fluid occupies a compact torus.

Independently, on $\mathbb T^2$, let $h:I\times\mathbb T^2\to(0,\infty)$ be total layer depth and $v:I\times\mathbb T^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be horizontal velocity. Let $g>0$ and $f\in\mathbb R$ be prescribed constants, define $Jv:=(-v_2,v_1)$, and take a fixed flat bottom. The inviscid one-layer shallow-water equation family is

$$h_t+\nabla\cdot(hv)=0,\qquad (hv)_t+\nabla\cdot(hv\otimes v)+\nabla\!\left(\frac{g h^2}{2}\right)+f h Jv=0.$$

The tensor divergence is rowwise, $(\nabla\cdot(hv\otimes v))_i=\sum_{j=1}^2\partial_{x_j}(h v_i v_j)$. This family has one layer, positive depth, a flat bottom, and no bottom friction, wetting/drying, or interlayer coupling. These are mathematical equation systems, not assertions that a measured fluid realizes them. With SI interpretation, $t$ is in seconds, spatial coordinates in metres, $u$ and $v$ in metres per second, $b$ in metres per second squared, $\pi$, $\Phi$, and $\Phi_{\rm eff}$ in square metres per square second, $f$, $N$, and $\Omega$ in inverse seconds, $\nu$ and $\kappa$ in square metres per second, $h$ in metres, and $g$ in metres per square second. The displayed coefficients are prescribed within these formulations; no empirical calibration is asserted. The energy integrals below omit a constant reference density; multiplying them by a specified density in kilograms per cubic metre gives joules.

references.title: Geoffrey K. Vallis, Fluid Dynamics of the Atmosphere and Ocean, University of Exeter lecture notes, Autumn 2018, §§1.6.2–1.6.3 and §2.4.2
Darryl D. Holm, Ideal shallow water dynamics in a rotating frame, Imperial College London MPE CDT PDE lecture notes, Autumn 2016, §§1.1 and 1.4
Paola Rizzoli, Wave Motion in the Ocean and the Atmosphere, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.802, Lecture 12: Shallow water equations with rotation — Poincaré waves, Spring 2008

items.title: Positive linear stratified energy and diffusion
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; cross-batch interfaces inspected, but the upstream supplier readiness record is missing.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and use the periodic domain $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with Lebesgue measure on $Q_3=[0,2\pi]^3$. Let $f\in\mathbb R$, $N>0$, and $\nu,\kappa\ge0$ be constants. Suppose $u,b$ are continuously differentiable in time and space with continuous second spatial derivatives, and $\pi$ has continuous first spatial derivatives; all fields are $2\pi$-periodic and satisfy

$$u_t+f e_3\times u+\nabla\pi=b e_3+\nu\Delta u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,\qquad b_t+N^2u_3=\kappa\Delta b.$$

Define the positive energy per reference density

$$E(t):=\frac12\int_{Q_3}\left(|u(t,x)|^2+\frac{b(t,x)^2}{N^2}\right)\,dx.$$

Then for every $t_0<t_1$ in $I$,

$$E(t_1)-E(t_0)=-\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\int_{Q_3}\left(\nu|\nabla u|^2+\frac{\kappa}{N^2}|\nabla b|^2\right)\,dx\,dt.$$

Thus the inviscid model conserves $E$, and the stated nonnegative diffusion coefficients make it nonincreasing. The condition $N>0$ is essential for this positive energy. This is an exact identity conditional on the displayed smooth linear Boussinesq equations; it is not a nonlinear or compressible stability theorem. A discrete analogue requires a skew Coriolis operator and compatible pressure/divergence pairing in the actual discretization; no claim is made for arbitrary schemes.

references.title: Geoffrey K. Vallis, Fluid Dynamics of the Atmosphere and Ocean, University of Exeter lecture notes, Autumn 2018, §1.6.3, equations (1.72)–(1.78)

items.title: Smooth rotating shallow-water energy balance
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; cross-batch interfaces inspected, but the upstream supplier readiness record is missing.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval and use $\mathbb T^2=\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ with Lebesgue measure on $Q_2=[0,2\pi]^2$. Let $h:I\times\mathbb T^2\to(0,\infty)$ and $v:I\times\mathbb T^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be continuously differentiable in time and space with continuous second spatial derivatives and $2\pi$-periodic lifts. Suppose they satisfy the one-layer rotating shallow-water equations with constant $f\in\mathbb R$, constant $g>0$, fixed flat bottom, and no friction:

$$h_t+\nabla\cdot(hv)=0,\qquad (hv)_t+\nabla\cdot(hv\otimes v)+\nabla\!\left(\frac{g h^2}{2}\right)+f h Jv=0,$$

where $J(v_1,v_2)=(-v_2,v_1)$. Define the normalized energy density per horizontal area by $E:=h|v|^2/2+gh^2/2$; it is per unit reference density, so a specified constant density converts its area integral to joules. Then the pointwise energy flux identity is

$$\partial_t E+\nabla\cdot\left(\left(E+\frac{gh^2}{2}\right)v\right)=0.$$

Consequently, for every $t_0<t_1$ in $I$,

$$\int_{Q_2}E(t_1,x)\,dx=\int_{Q_2}E(t_0,x)\,dx.$$

This is an exact smooth identity for the stated adopted equation system, not an aspect-ratio or hydrostatic-error estimate and not a positivity guarantee for an arbitrary discretization. Bottom topography, wetting/drying, bottom friction, or multiple layers require separately defined systems and their corresponding energy terms.

references.title: Geoffrey K. Vallis, Fluid Dynamics of the Atmosphere and Ocean, University of Exeter lecture notes, Autumn 2018, §2.4.2, equations (2.55)–(2.59)
Darryl D. Holm, Ideal shallow water dynamics in a rotating frame, Imperial College London MPE CDT PDE lecture notes, Autumn 2016, §§1.1 and 1.4, equations (1.1) and (1.14)
Paola Rizzoli, Wave Motion in the Ocean and the Atmosphere, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.802, Lecture 12: Shallow water equations with rotation — Poincaré waves, Spring 2008

items.title: Resting depth and stratification states
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; cross-batch interfaces inspected, but the upstream supplier readiness record is missing.
items.statement: Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval. For $d=2,3$, let $\mathbb T^d:=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ and represent fields by $2\pi$-periodic lifts, integrating over $Q_d=[0,2\pi]^d$ with Lebesgue measure. For any constants $f\in\mathbb R$, $N>0$, and $\nu,\kappa\ge0$, the fields $u=b=\pi=0$ on $I\times\mathbb T^3$ solve the rotating linear stratified equations and have $E_s=\frac12\int_{Q_3}(|u|^2+b^2/N^2)\,dx=0$. For any constants $f\in\mathbb R$, $g>0$, and $H>0$, the fields $h\equiv H$, $v\equiv0$ on $I\times\mathbb T^2$ solve the one-layer rotating shallow-water equations and have normalized total energy $E_h=\int_{Q_2}(h|v|^2/2+gh^2/2)\,dx=2\pi^2gH^2$. Both are stationary smooth periodic states of the stated mathematical systems, not observed fluid states.

references.title: Geoffrey K. Vallis, Fluid Dynamics of the Atmosphere and Ocean, University of Exeter lecture notes, Autumn 2018, §§1.6.3 and 2.4.2
